transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-12-15
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Nina Gomez (CTO - AcmeAI), Ravi Singh (ML Eng), Sara Lopez (SRE)

[00:00] Laura (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Laura, I'll run the demo, Marcus will jump into the parity details. Nina, Ravi, Sara, thanks for taking time.
[00:12] Nina (AcmeAI): Thanks Laura, yeah we want to see how close Redwood is to OpenAI/Anthropic/Together for our existing integration. Main goals are parity, lower cost, and options for private networking.
[00:22] Marcus (Redwood): Great, quick agenda: high-level API mapping, streaming and function/tool calling differences, embeddings migration, and then a quick Console/Optimize walkthrough. We'll leave time for Q&A.
[00:34] Ravi (AcmeAI): Sounds good. We have two main workloads — chat assistant (few-shot, lots of function calls) and embeddings for similarity search.
[00:40] Marcus: Perfect, we'll show both. First, API parity: Redwood exposes a single REST endpoint for generation and chat, with model param names that map to OpenAI/Anthropic names. For example, openai "gpt-4o-mini" maps to redwood model alias "rw-g4o-mini" in our catalog. Temperature/top_p and max_tokens map 1:1, but we add a couple of Redwood-specific opts for batching and prefix/KV caching.
[01:05] Nina: When you say function calling — is that the same schema we use with OpenAI? We rely on structured JSON output from functions.
[01:12] Marcus: Yes, we support function/tool calling; the payload is very similar. There are small differences in event types for the stream — e.g., our stream emits an intermediate "tool_request" event when a tool is invoked, which some parsers need to handle. We'll share sample SDK snippets.
[01:28] Laura: I'll put those in the parity doc. One thing to flag: Anthropic's response style, the safety layers, sometimes change how prompts are framed; we recommend a short normalization pass for role/assistant tags during migration.
[01:45] Ravi: Okay, that makes sense. For embeddings — we use OpenAI's text-embedding-3-small for production. How similar are Redwood embeddings?
[01:53] Marcus: Redwood provides curated open-model embeddings and we've verified cosine-similarity parity for common tasks. We'll include an eval result in the doc, but expect marginal differences; we also support reindexing helpers and batch-embedding endpoints to reduce round trips.
[02:10] Sara: What about streaming? Our product uses streaming for token-by-token UI updates; latency is critical.
[02:17] Marcus: Streaming is supported. Note that because Redwood routes requests through optimized continuous-batching runtime, you might see slightly different tail latencies depending on batch size. We offer per-route SLOs and can pin workloads to Dedicated pools for predictable latency.
[02:34] Nina: Dedicated vs hosted — cost tradeoffs? We currently pay a lot for tokens on OpenAI, if we move to Redwood hosted API do we get cost savings or only with Dedicated?
[02:43] Laura: For most customers, hosted gives immediate savings through model catalog and batching; Dedicated/reserved capacity unlocks larger cost reductions and predictable throughput. We'll share a sample cost model comparing typical OpenAI bill to Redwood hosted and Dedicated.
[03:00] Ravi: Any rough numbers now?
[03:02] Laura: Roughly, depending on model and quantization profiles, customers see 20-50% reduction on token cost on hosted and up to ~60% with Dedicated + quantized model variants. Those are example numbers — we'll run a benchmark with your load to provide concrete figures.
[03:20] Sara: Security — we're regulated, need SSO, audit logs, SOC 2, KMS, and possibly on-prem. How does Redwood handle that?
[03:28] Marcus: Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) supports customer-managed control plane options, KMS/HSM integrations, SAML/SSO, RBAC, and long-retention audit logs. We have SOC 2 Type II compliance; I'll send the security pack.
[03:44] Nina: Great. For the POC we'll need to run some performance tests — our key metrics are 95th percentile latency < 250ms for short completions, and embedding throughput of 1k/sec for batch windows. Can Redwood meet those?
[03:58] Marcus: We can with Dedicated pools and tuned batching. We'll validate on your sample workload during the POC. A two-day bench run is typical to get representative numbers.
[04:12] Laura: We'll also show the Console quickly — Optimize recommendations for batching and quantization, and how cost/latency tradeoffs surface in the UI.
[04:20] Marcus: Quick share screen? (screen share) Okay, here is the Console — per-route analytics, token breakdown, and the Optimize tab which suggests batching sizes and quant profiles. You can pin a rollout to a model variant and set automatic fallback to hosted if Dedicated is saturated.
[04:40] Nina: Nice, can we run a canary during rollout?
[04:43] Marcus: Yes, canary and A/B. You can define traffic splits and automatic rollback conditions.
[04:50] Ravi: On the SDK side, how much code change? We use Python and Node.
[04:55] Marcus: Minimal — our SDKs mirror popular OpenAI client signatures. Example: openai.ChatCompletion.create maps to redwood.client.chat.create with nearly identical kwargs. We'll send sample snippets that show 2-3 lines changed for auth and model name.
[05:10] Nina: Any gotchas for TogetherAI users? We use together's models for smaller cheap inference currently.
[05:17] Laura: Together has a slightly different API for streaming and rate limits; Redwood has explicit rate limits per-tenant, and our routing layer can route to cheaper model variants for low-stakes workloads. We'll include mapping for Together model names.
[05:32] (snippets and small cross talk)
[05:40] Ravi: About data retention — we have to ensure no customer data is used for model training.
[05:44] Marcus: By default Redwood doesn't use customer data to train public models; for Hosted we have options for retention settings and contractual clauses. Private/on-prem gives you full control over data residency. Security doc will include the retention policy options.
[06:00] Sara: For VPC peering, what ports and egress rules?
[06:04] Marcus: We'll provide a network spec. Typically we only need outbound HTTPS to certain endpoints and a few control-plane ports; we'll get precise firewall rules in the doc.
[06:14] Nina: Ok, let's talk timeline. We want to decide before end of Q1 (end of March). POC needs to happen in next two weeks ideally.
[06:22] Laura: We can target a POC the week of 2025-12-22 if you can get sample data to us this week. That gives your execs initial numbers to review before Q1.
[06:33] Ravi: We'll try to upload prompts and traffic profile by Thursday.
[06:36] Nina: Want a cost/latency spreadsheet too — to present to CFO.
[06:40] Laura: We'll include a template.
[06:45] Marcus: Quick demo note — here's an example of the parity mapping table (reading): OpenAI param "model" -> Redwood "model", "temperature" -> "temperature", "max_tokens" -> "max_tokens". Function call schema maps but watch for stream event names ("tool_request"). For embeddings, you can call "redwood.embeddings.create" with identical input arrays.
[07:05] Ravi: (laughs) good. Any sample code for bulk-embedding?
[07:08] Marcus: Yes — batch endpoint and upload via multipart. The SDK will do that behind the scenes, but sample curl/py/node included in the doc.
[07:18] Nina: If we need on-prem, what's the gating?
[07:21] Laura: On-prem requires deeper infra review, but we've done air-gapped installs for regulated customers. That's typically an enterprise/licensing conversation. We'll put that in the security pack and SOW template.
[07:35] (short pause, typing noises)
[07:44] Sara: Alright. I have one more SRE question: KV cache behavior — we rely on long-lived KV caches across requests to speed up dialog. Any differences?
[07:53] Marcus: Redwood's runtime supports KV cache preservation across requests when you pin a session; it's configurable. There are some limits based on memory and model architecture, we'll document recommended sizes. Occasionally transcription shows K-V as K V cash in auto transcripts, but it's the same thing.
[08:14] Nina: Okay that answers a lot. Let's recap next steps.
[08:18] Laura: Recap: Redwood to send parity mapping doc, SDK snippets, pricing + Dedicated sizing spreadsheet, and security pack. Acme to provide sample prompts, traffic, and network constraints. We'll schedule a two-day POC bench the week of 2025-12-22.
[08:33] Nina: That works. Any final questions?
[08:36] Ravi: Not from me.
[08:38] Sara: No, thanks.
[08:40] Laura: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with links.
[08:44] Nina: Thanks, bye.

Notes: transcription contains minor auto-transcribe errors (e.g., "K V cash" vs "KV cache", some speaker labels simplified). References: parity mapping doc (link to be shared), pricing spreadsheet (link to be shared), security pack (link).
